ECG_Clinical_Summary.title: ECG Digital Twin Dataset - Signal-Level Statistical Report
overview: This report summarizes the signal-level statistical characteristics of the ECG digital twin dataset, comprising 12 recording sessions captured between January and June 2026. Each entry in the source dataset represents a single-channel ECG waveform recorded from the digital twin data stream, described only in terms of amplitude distribution (minimum, maximum, mean, median, standard deviation, and percentiles).

dataset_summary.channel_configuration: single channel ("ECG SD") in every recording

notable_observations: All 12 recordings use a single channel sampled at 256 Hz, so statistics are directly comparable across sessions.
Recording duration varies considerably, from about 1h 11m (2026-04-11) to about 22h 27m (2026-03-25).

The 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-29 recordings have matching percentile values and near-identical histogram shapes, suggesting very similar signal characteristics or a data duplication between the two sessions.
Standard deviation of amplitude ranges from about 82.6 uV (2026-01-03) to about 303.1 uV (2026-05-05), indicating substantially different signal variability/noise levels between sessions.
Peak-to-peak amplitude (max minus min) ranges from roughly 2,480 uV (2026-05-25) to about 3,470 uV (2026-05-05).
ECG_Clinical_Summary.scope_and_limitations: This report is derived strictly from the statistical fields present in the source dataset. It does not represent a clinical or diagnostic ECG interpretation. Any assessment of cardiac rhythm, heart rate, or abnormality requires review of the underlying waveform by a qualified clinician or an appropriately validated diagnostic algorithm, neither of which is reflected in this report.

overall_observation.observation: Longitudinal EEG recordings demonstrate a consistent transition from stable interictal activity to preictal electrical instability followed by high-amplitude ictal seizure activity.
supporting_evidence: Signal variance progressively increases before seizure onset.
Amplitude increases significantly during ictal recordings.
Electrical activity returns toward baseline following seizure events.
Temporal seizure progression remains consistent across six months.
overall_observation.clinical_interpretation: Findings are consistent with chronic recurrent epilepsy exhibiting reproducible seizure evolution.
overall_observation.digital_twin_interpretation: EEG features provide sufficient longitudinal information to model baseline, transition, seizure, and recovery states for personalized neurological Digital Twin generation.

longitudinal_summary.overall_clinical_status: Stable with intermittent exacerbations followed by recovery

clinical_progression.summary: Partial seizure control with preserved cognition and normal laboratory findings.
Reduced seizure count but prolonged seizure duration and seizure clustering increased short-term neurological risk.
Clinical stabilization with normal CBC and no evidence of cognitive deterioration.
Highest seizure burden during follow-up despite stable medication regimen.
Shorter seizure duration, improved mental clarity and recovery from previous deterioration.

disease_behavior.pattern: Fluctuating chronic epilepsy with episodic worsening

seizure_analysis.overall_pattern: Persistent focal epilepsy with intermittent exacerbations
seizure_analysis.overall_inference: Seizure burden fluctuates over time without continuous deterioration. Final visit demonstrates improved seizure duration suggesting partial therapeutic response.

aura_analysis.clinical_significance: Aura characteristics remain consistent across visits indicating stable seizure onset localization.
aura_analysis.digital_twin_use: Useful biomarker for future seizure prediction.

medication_response.overall_inference: Current regimen provides acceptable seizure suppression while maintaining favorable safety profile.

sleep_analysis.clinical_relationship: Improved sleep corresponds with reduced seizure duration during later visits.

cognitive_analysis.overall_inference: No evidence of progressive cognitive impairment throughout observation.

quality_of_life.overall_inference: Despite persistent seizures, patient maintains satisfactory functional independence.

recommended_actions: Track seizure triggers and aura characteristics.
Continue periodic CBC and liver function monitoring.
Assess treatment escalation only if seizure frequency increases further.

If seizure frequency increases and escalation is considered, prioritize SCN1A-aligned options (clobazam, ethosuximide, oxcarbazepine) over valproic acid, carbamazepine, or phenytoin, per integrated pharmacogenomic profile.

Should any psychiatric comorbidity (depression/anxiety) require treatment, avoid paroxetine given dual genetic suicidality flags (FKBP5, HTR1B); consider lithium given its concordant favorable efficacy signal.

genomics_integration.summary: SCN1A-favorable allele supports both current anti-epileptic drugs (levetiracetam, lamotrigine); CYP3A4 (TT) partially offsets the lamotrigine signal, consistent with observed moderate-not-complete seizure control. Valproic acid, carbamazepine, and phenytoin are genetically weaker escalation options and should be deprioritized in favor of clobazam, ethosuximide, or oxcarbazepine if the regimen must change.
psychiatric_safety_flags_on_file: FKBP5 (rs1360780) — avoid/monitor clomipramine, lithium (caution only, efficacy signal is favorable), nefazodone, paroxetine, venlafaxine

executive_summary.clinical_conclusion: Across five follow-up visits, the patient demonstrated a fluctuating but overall stable epilepsy course. Although one transient exacerbation resulted in increased seizure burden, neurological function, cognition, laboratory safety, and daily functioning remained preserved. Improvement during the final visit suggests continued benefit from the existing anti-epileptic regimen. The Digital Twin currently classifies the patient as having moderately controlled chronic epilepsy with moderate future seizure risk and favorable long-term prognosis under continued monitoring. Newly integrated pharmacogenomic data reinforces this picture at the molecular level: the current Levetiracetam/Lamotrigine regimen is the panel's best-aligned option, carrying a supportive SCN1A signal and no toxicity flag, while a partially offsetting CYP3A4 signal on lamotrigine helps explain the observed moderate (not complete) seizure control. Should treatment escalation or a psychiatric comorbidity ever arise, the genomic profile also flags valproic acid, carbamazepine, and phenytoin as weaker efficacy options, and paroxetine specifically as carrying a dual genetic suicidality signal — information now available for proactive, rather than reactive, prescribing decisions.
